title: docs(types,objectql,runtime,cli): repoint the degraded-boot stderr copy at the reason that survived #4012
body:
Close-out of #4012 (fixed in #4084). Comment/test-name only — **no behavior changes**.

## What I set out to do, and why I didn't

#4012 noted that plugins had visibly worked around the swallowed log sink by bypassing the logger, and that this was "a tell that the sink has been quietly unusable for a while". `emitDegradedBootBanner` is that workaround, and its doc comment described the bug verbatim:

> *"`OS_ALLOW_DRIVER_CONNECT_FAILURE` only justifies itself if the state it opts into is impossible to miss — and a logger-only banner is missable: `os serve` swallows ALL of stdout while the kernel boots (its "boot-quiet" capture), and `Logger` routes `warn` to stdout, so the one message that matters would be invisible in exactly the situation it exists for."*

So the plan was to retire the duplicate now that #4084 fixed the sink. **On inspection that would have been a regression**, and the reason is worth stating plainly:

```ts
private write(level: LogLevel, message: string, …) {
    if (!this.isEnabled(level)) return;      // ← core/src/logger.ts
```

`logger.warn` is dropped **before touching any stream** when the level is below `config.level`. At `--log-level error`, `fatal`, or `silent` the banner reaches *no* stream — and a production host at `error` is exactly the deployment `OS_ALLOW_DRIVER_CONNECT_FAILURE` exists for. The stderr copy was always load-bearing; it was load-bearing for a **different reason than the one written down**, and #4012 removed only the reason.

That is the failure mode AGENTS.md warns about — a stale premise fossilized in a comment — pointed the other way: the next person reads "this exists because of boot-quiet", sees boot-quiet fixed, and deletes it.

## The change

Repoint the justification everywhere someone would read it before deleting the helper:

- `packages/types/src/degraded-boot.ts` — the level filter is now the stated reason, with an explicit *"do not re-derive this helper's necessity from the boot-quiet capture"*.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` — the emit-site comment no longer points at the boot window.
- **all three parity tests** renamed off *"which `os serve` boot-quiet cannot swallow"* → *"which the operator log level cannot filter away"*: `objectql/src/engine-driver-connect-failfast.test.ts`, `runtime/src/degraded-boot-parity.test.ts`, `service-datasource/src/__tests__/datasource-connection-service.test.ts`.

The objectql test now **proves** the claim instead of asserting around it — it previously passed a no-op logger, so it would have passed whatever the level filter did:

```ts
logger: new ObjectLogger({ level: 'error' }),   // a REAL logger, silenced as a prod host silences it
…
expect(written.join('')).toContain('DEGRADED BOOT');        // stderr carries it
expect(onStdout.join('')).not.toContain('DEGRADED BOOT');   // …and the logger emitted nothing
```

Verified the pin has teeth: flipping that level to `warn` fails the second assertion (`expected '…WARN ⚠️ DEGR…' not to contain 'DEGRADED BOOT'`).

## Same sweep, same class of stale premise

Three more places overstated what #4012 had not yet fixed. Each artifact stays — only the reason changes, to the one that is still true:

- **Automation wiring summary** (`format.ts`, `serve.ts`, `serve-automation-summary.test.ts`) claimed the boot window swallowed the engine's binding warnings. Its real justification is *stronger* and untouched by #4012: a flow that silently fails to arm emits **no log line at any level**, so binding state has to be read off the live engine. Absence of a warning was never evidence of a bound flow.
- **Seed summary** (`seed-summary.ts`, `format.ts`, `format.seed-summary.test.ts`) and **`AppPlugin`'s seed-outcome note** attributed the silence to the boot window; the operative gate is that `SeedLoader`'s result logs are `info`, under the default `warn`.

## Verification

| package | result |
|---|---|
| `@objectstack/objectql` | 80 files / 1180 tests ✅ |
| `@objectstack/runtime` | 64/65 files, 913/914 ✅ — one **pre-existing** failure, see below |
| `@objectstack/types` | 48 ✅ |
| `@objectstack/cli` | 84 files / 877 ✅ |
| `service-datasource` | 154 ✅ |

`eslint` clean on all eleven touched files.

The runtime failure (`datasource-autoconnect.test.ts`, federated read returns 8 duplicated rows for 2 seeded) reproduces with this diff stashed, on clean `main`, both alone and in-suite — and CI's Test Core was green on #4084, so it looks environment-sensitive. Not mine; filed as #4102. Worth noting one non-finding: an earlier run also failed `plugin.integration.test.ts`, which turned out to be nothing but a stale `dist/` on my side — it passes 43/43 after a rebuild.
